nodes.name: ParquetAdapter
nodes.summary: Discovers Parquet inputs and exposes their schema and records as a normalized row stream through bounded record batches.

nodes.summary: Implements read-only workbook discovery and row streaming with sheet-alias resolution, optional removal of unnamed leading columns, and registry-based adapter dispatch.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the operational overview to understand ehr2cdm's purpose: deterministic conversion of local EHR exports into a lineage-preserving canonical layer, then OMOP CDM 5.4 and MEDS. The README also establishes the project's safety boundaries—uncertain rows are quarantined, semantic proposals require human confirmation, and protected data stays local.

tour.title: CLI and Orchestration
tour.description: With the end-to-end workflow in view, follow the Typer CLI that exposes inspection, ingestion, canonicalization, publication, validation, review, and tracing commands. The run coordinator executes stage tasks reproducibly, while centralized paths and version fingerprints make parallel work resumable and content-addressed.
tour.languageLesson: Typer turns annotated Python functions into CLI commands, while dataclasses and process executors keep orchestration state explicit and serializable. Context managers around run metadata ensure completion and failure details are recorded consistently.

tour.title: Dataset Contracts
tour.description: Before any patient data is read, strict Pydantic models define what a dataset must declare about files, identities, timestamps, anchors, and publication policy. The CTPE and generic fixtures show that hospital-specific semantics live in YAML rather than core code, while the environment template separates protected input and output locations from versioned configuration.
tour.languageLesson: YAML expresses dataset-specific policy, but Pydantic performs the actual validation and rejects unknown or unsafe settings. This keeps configuration declarative without making it permissive.

tour.title: Discovery and Ingestion
tour.description: Building on those contracts, discovery inventories raw partitions, resolves logical sources, and surfaces unanswered owner decisions before conversion begins. Format-neutral adapter contracts then let delimited and Excel readers stream original values into content-addressed source Parquet while ingestion attaches row-level hashes, lineage, quarantine records, and an immutable manifest.
tour.languageLesson: Python iterators and generators allow adapters to stream rows instead of loading an export into memory. Protocol-style interfaces keep physical file handling replaceable while preserving one logical row contract.

tour.title: Identity and Determinism
tour.description: Once source rows exist, identity resolution joins patient keys across partitions before any clinical normalization occurs. Canonical serialization and cryptographic hashing produce stable subject IDs, event IDs, worker buckets, and dataset splits, so changing process count or row order cannot change the meaning of the output.

tour.title: Canonical Data Contracts
tour.description: The canonical layer begins with frozen Arrow and Pydantic schemas that define clinical facts, lineage links, anchors, quality issues, and quarantine rows. Time parsing accepts only declared formats and timezone policy, while value parsing distinguishes numbers, ranges, comparators, sentinel text, and unsafe values instead of coercing them.

tour.title: Canonical Event Building
tour.description: Using the contracts from the previous step, registered row shapes turn source roles into events, lineage links, issues, and quarantine records. Anchor logic keeps extraction provenance out of the clinical clock, deterministic deduplication collapses repeated facts without losing source links, and the builder stages subjects into buckets before publishing globally sorted canonical tables.

tour.title: OMOP Publication
tour.description: The OMOP publisher projects canonical facts into CDM 5.4 clinical and audit tables while preserving source values, identity mappings, terminology decisions, and lineage. The pinned DuckDB DDL plus primary- and foreign-key migrations make the target contract concrete and allow validation to inspect the artifact that actually ships.
tour.languageLesson: SQL DDL fixes column types and nullability, while separate constraint scripts express primary and foreign keys. Keeping these artifacts versioned makes schema drift visible and reproducible.

tour.title: MEDS Publication
tour.description: In parallel with OMOP, the MEDS publisher derives deterministic subject shards, code metadata, dataset metadata, splits, and availability-aware event views from the same canonical truth. The generated MEDS 0.4.1 reference explains the exact filesystem and column contract, including the project's available-time extension for leakage-safe modeling.

tour.title: Human Semantic Review
tour.description: After deterministic parsing and publication rules are established, terminology resolution performs exact and candidate-based vocabulary matching and sends unresolved semantics into a governed review registry. A guarded local LLM may rank retrieved candidates under a constrained prompt, but only accepted human decisions compile into mappings that can affect OMOP or MEDS output.

tour.title: Validation and Lineage
tour.description: Validation spans manifests, reconciliation, identity, canonical semantics, OMOP constraints, MEDS schemas, lineage completeness, sharding, and leakage rather than trusting successful execution. Patient tracing reconstructs individual records across every layer, while controlled fault injections and their catalogue demonstrate which checks catch historically realistic silent corruption.

tour.title: Tests and CI
tour.description: The tour concludes with PHI-free integration tests that prove YAML-only generalization, worker-count determinism, resumption, OMOP/MEDS publication, and the absence of fabricated or leaking facts. GitHub Actions runs the supported Python matrix, excludes protected real-data tests, enforces dataset generality, and gates changes on the fault-detection experiment.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions YAML uses triggers, jobs, matrix expansion, and ordered steps to turn repository policy into an executable quality gate. The workflow separates portable synthetic checks from tests that require local protected data.
